body_markdown:
The Venice International Film Festival takes place Sept. 2-12, 2026, on the Lido di Venezia. For business aviation operators, the primary planning challenge is aircraft parking at Venice Marco Polo Airport (LIPZ), where parking during the Festival will be limited to 24 hours.


LIPZ remains the preferred airport because of its proximity to Venice and direct access to water transportation, but operators planning stays longer than 24 hours should build a repositioning strategy into the mission from the outset.


## What operators need to know for 2026


- LIPZ requires PPR for GA operations, with parking approval incorporated into the PPR process.
- During the Film Festival, aircraft parking at LIPZ will be limited to 24 hours.
- Parking requests are prioritized based on when they are received. Requests made less than two hours before arrival may not receive a stand except for quick-turn operations.
- Operational handling information is expected 36 hours before scheduled arrival.
- LIPZ normally operates 0600-2200 local.
- Treviso (LIPH) and Trieste (LIPQ) are the closest practical repositioning alternatives.
- Milan Linate (LIML) is another option when parking availability is the priority.
- Passenger transportation requires additional coordination because movement between LIPZ, Venice and the Lido often depends on water taxis rather than conventional ground transportation.
- No aviation-related strikes or other major disruptions are currently expected during the event. A rail strike announced for Sept. 7 is not expected to affect business aviation operations.
